title: A rank-one projective module whose K_0 class is a multiple of [S] is trivial
statement: Let $S$ be a commutative ring and let $L$ be a finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] $S$-module such that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ the localization $L_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is a free [def-weil-pbc-free-module] $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module of rank one. If $[L]=n[S]$ in $K_0(S)$ [def-trf-k0-group] for some integer $n$, then $L\cong S$ as $S$-modules.

source.place: Lemma 0AFX (more-algebra-lemma-det), line 36463: det: K_0(R) -> Pic(R) with det[M] = wedge^n M for M finite locally free of rank n (here det[L]=L and det(n[S])=S), read with Lemma 0B8I (more-algebra-lemma-invertible), line 36118, identifying L with an invertible module; as used in the last sentence of the proof of Tag 0AFZ, line 36796

proof.text: Use $K_0(S)$ in the current presentation [def-trf-k0-group]: its generators are isomorphism classes of finite projective quotients $S^m/N$, with the direct-sum relations $[Q']+[Q'']=[Q'\oplus Q'']$. These are the classes and group in [lem-trf-k0-determinant-map], so no change of K-group is involved. The hypotheses on $L$ are exactly those of its rank-one clause. It therefore identifies $\det([L])$ with the Picard class represented by $L$. The module $S$ is finite free of rank one, hence is finite projective and is free of rank one after every prime localization; the same statement identifies $\det([S])$ with the identity Picard class represented by $S$.

source.place: Lemma 0AFX (more-algebra-lemma-det), line 36463, specialized to rank one

proof.text: Write the Picard group multiplicatively. Apply the group homomorphism $\det$ to the assumed equality $[L]=n[S]$ in this $K_0(S)$. Its homomorphism law gives $\det([L])=\det([S])^n=1^n=1$ for every integer $n$, including zero and negative integers. Since the Picard group in [lem-trf-k0-determinant-map] consists of isomorphism classes of modules and its identity class is represented by $S$, equality of the classes of $L$ and $S$ means exactly $L\cong S$ as $S$-modules.
